title: Importing Modules with import knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the central idea of “Importing Modules with import”?
options: A module is a Python source file whose names can be imported by other code.
A command that installs all third-party packages without checking dependencies.
A guarantee that any Python program is secure and portable.
A replacement for tests, documentation, and runtime verification.
questions.answer_key: A module is a Python source file whose names can be imported by other code.
questions.explanation: The lesson focuses on this principle: A module is a Python source file whose names can be imported by other code. The other options describe unrelated or unsafe assumptions.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when learning or applying “Importing Modules with import”?
options: Ignore errors and assume the first output is correct.
Change several unrelated parts until the program appears to work.
Test a small case, inspect the result, and consult the versioned reference when behavior differs.
Always use the newest syntax regardless of the project’s supported Python versions.
questions.answer_key: Test a small case, inspect the result, and consult the versioned reference when behavior differs.
questions.explanation: Small, repeatable tests and versioned references help distinguish a misunderstanding from a runtime or compatibility difference.

questions.prompt: When a result related to “Importing Modules with import” differs from what you expected, what is the strongest first debugging step?
options: Reduce the case, inspect the inputs and traceback or current state, check the supported Python version, and retest one change at a time.
Add unrelated changes until the output looks plausible.
Suppress all exceptions without understanding their cause.
Assume that any unexpected result proves Python itself is broken.
questions.answer_key: Reduce the case, inspect the inputs and traceback or current state, check the supported Python version, and retest one change at a time.
questions.explanation: A small reproducible case makes it easier to identify whether the input, logic, runtime version, or environment caused the difference. Change one factor and rerun before layering on fixes.
